An MP asked the Prime Minister whether the frigate Van Nes escorted US weapons shipments for the 2003 Iraq invasion, whether a file on this was withheld from the Davids inquiry, and whether a Dutch Special Forces colonel was placed at US Central Command. The government answered that the information was available to the Davids inquiry, that the frigate did not breach its rules of engagement, and that the colonel's liaison posting had no role in Iraq operations, while declining to share the file with the Chamber beyond what was already provided.
The information has been shared with the Davids committee and the Chamber.
De informatie is gedeeld met de commissie Davids en de Kamer.

Vragen van het lid Van Bommel (SP) aan de minister-president, minister van Algemene Zaken, over uitlatingen van de voormalige minister van Buitenlandse Zaken De Hoop Scheffer over het onderzoek naar de steun aan de oorlo

Parliamentarian Van Bommel asks the Prime Minister whether the former foreign minister De Hoop Scheffer's call for a public inquiry into Dutch support for the Iraq war and for publication of his conversation with the Davids Commission is shared, and whether the interview records will be released. The Prime Minister answers that the commission was free to set its own method and chose a closed inquiry, and that the interview records will not be published to protect confidentiality promised to witnesses and their privacy.
I will not make the interview records public.
De gespreksverslagen maak ik niet openbaar.

Vragen van het lid Van Bommel (SP) aan de minister-president, minister van Algemene Zaken, over uitlatingen van de voormalige minister van Buitenlandse Zaken De Hoop Scheffer over het onderzoek naar de steun aan de oorlo

An SP MP asks the Prime Minister whether he noticed former foreign minister De Hoop Scheffer's remarks that he favoured a parliamentary inquiry into Dutch support for the Iraq war and that the Davids Commission interview report could be public, whether he agrees the inquiry should have been public, and whether he will make the interview reports public. The government replies only that answering needs more time than three weeks and that answers will follow as soon as possible.

I hereby inform you that answering the questions from MP Van Bommel (SP) about remarks by former foreign minister De Hoop Scheffer on the investigation into support for the Iraq war requires more time than the three-week period, given the necessary deliberation and coordination.

Hierbij laat ik u weten dat de beantwoording van de vragen van het lid Van Bommel (SP) over uitlatingen van de voormalige minister van Buitenlandse Zaken De Hoop Scheffer over het onderzoek naar de steun aan de oorlog in Irak (kenmerk 2010Z07516 ), gezien de noodzakelijke afweging en afstemming meer tijd vergt dan de termijn van drie weken.
Vragen van het lid Van Raak (SP) aan de minister-president, minister van Algemene Zaken, over de kosten voor het onderhoud van het jacht de Groene Draeck (ingezonden 19 februari 2010).

MP Van Raak (SP) asked how the maintenance and restoration costs of the royal yacht De Groene Draeck were calculated, whether independent experts were consulted, and whether an independent inquiry will be held. The Prime Minister replied that maintenance costs are based on a 2008 benchmark (EUR 47,000), that restoration is estimated at EUR 326,000 pending dismantling and assessment by Defence experts, and that no independent inquiry is planned, referring to the earlier answers.

Halsema (GroenLinks) asked the Prime Minister and Defence Minister whether the Davids Commission on the Iraq invasion can access all information, including what former MPs of the intelligence oversight committee received, whether ministers who sat on that committee should be released from confidentiality, and whether Dutch intelligence cooperation with the US, Germany and France in gathering Iraq intelligence should be investigated. The government's supplementary answer says questions 8 to 11 are addressed in the Davids Commission report (section 9.6), and that intelligence cooperation between the US and other countries was not examined by that commission (question 12).
Intelligence cooperation between the US and other countries in the intelligence field was not a subject of investigation by the Commission of Inquiry into Iraq decision-making.
De inlichtingensamenwerking tussen de VS en andere landen op inlichtingengebied is geen onderwerp van onderzoek geweest van de commissie van onderzoek besluitvorming Irak.

MPs Van der Ham and Halsema asked the Prime Minister about claims in a book on Prince Bernhard, including whether royal and intelligence archive documents should be transferred to public archives, whether undisclosed documents remain, and whether the Archives Act should be amended or NIOD should investigate. The government declined to react to the claims, stated the Royal Household archive is private and that no relevant documents are held by Algemene Zaken, and said existing archive and transparency rules are adequate with no need to amend the Archives Act.
The Royal Household archive is a private archive.
Het Koninklijk Huisarchief is een particulier archief.

qa: Antwoord op vragen van de leden Ünver en Maij over het bericht dat in Turkije geen televisieberichtgeving over aanslagen is toegestaan

MPs Ünver and Maij asked the Foreign Minister about a reported Turkish ban on television coverage of terrorist attacks, its legality, Turkey's wider press freedom restrictions, and Dutch action in the Council of Europe and ECtHR. The minister confirmed the ban was government-ordered during the state of emergency, listed journalist detentions and media closures, and described Dutch support for independent Turkish media and Council of Europe engagement.
By issuing this instruction from the government, Turkish media are, in the period immediately following an attack, only permitted to pass on official government communications to the public.

Met het van overheidswege uitvaardigen van deze instructie wordt het Turkse media in de periode direct volgend op een aanslag uitsluitend nog toegestaan om officiële regeringsmededelingen door te geven aan het publiek.
Antwoord op vragen van de leden Maij en Ünver over de blokkade van de website en app van de NOS in Turkije

MPs Maij and Ünver asked the Foreign Minister about the Turkish blocking of NOS website and app, its cause, the government's response, and whether Turkey's press freedom is being restricted. The minister replied that the Netherlands objected to Turkish authorities and requested clarification, that the block followed NOS publishing footage of the Russian ambassador's murder and was upheld by a court, and that press freedom is raised regularly in bilateral and EU contexts.
The Netherlands has, following the blocking, objected to the Turkish authorities and requested clarification.
Nederland heeft naar aanleiding van de blokkade bezwaar aangetekend bij de Turkse autoriteiten en om opheldering gevraagd.
